A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JavisDiT work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, component and loss ablations, audio-generation results, and JavisScore validation in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds a human preference study, duration evaluations, latency measurements and further analyses.

M1.justification: The DiT branches, hierarchical priors, contrastive losses, rectified-flow inference and conditional masking mechanism remain. Renaming ablation components from ST-SA/ST-CA to STDiT/HiST-Sypo does not introduce a different architecture. Withdrawing conditional-generation demonstrations does not establish an altered generation algorithm.

E1.justification: The training datasets and main benchmarks remain, but demonstrated conditional-task coverage contracts substantially. v1 Appendix F.2 and Figure A11 evaluate audio/video conditioning, image conditioning and audiovisual continuation; those demonstrations disappear, and v2 Appendix E.7 describes integration of these tasks as future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds UniVerse-1 to the JavisBench comparison and evaluates it in the new human study. Metric-validation Table A5 adds DeSync and its tie-inclusive variant, although the accompanying prose names SynchFormer. The earlier comparator sets otherwise remain.

E3.justification: The reported stage-1 budget changes from 13 epochs to 55 epochs (v1 Table A1; v2 Table A2), although v1 already included 55-epoch audio results. New protocols include 4-second versus 10-second generation evaluations, blind preference judgments on 100 prompts by three volunteers, and tie-inclusive accuracy for the additional synchronization comparator. These changes do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostics with generation-length comparisons, component latency profiling, a training-prompt distribution visualization, and a sequential-event attention case study. It also supplies individual metrics for existing ablations. The original component, loss and metric-sensitivity analyses remain, while the X-conditional generation case study is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging the new human study's three annotators is part of its evaluation protocol, without accompanying uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 becomes v2 Table 1, replacing JavisDiT's FVD/FAD/JavisScore of 203.2/6.9/0.158 with 204.1/7.2/0.154. Baseline alignment scores, ablation scores and JavisBench-mini audio results also change. v2 adds comparator, human-study, duration, latency and detailed ablation results, while removing conditional-generation examples. Closed-set benchmark and 10-second AudioCaps results remain unchanged. The revised training budget prevents interpreting all updates as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 adds mathematical attention-complexity analysis, contrasting O((THW)^2) with O(THW(T+HW)). The task definitions, prior and loss equations, and JavisScore formulation remain unchanged; no substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central JavisDiT, HiST-Sypo, JavisBench and synchronization-metric contributions, including broad superiority claims, remain. v2 Section 4.1 adds the explicit novelty claim that JavisBench is the first evaluation benchmark focused on multi-event synchronization.

C2.justification: v2 adds backbone and representation-gap explanations for the tradeoff against UniVerse-1, discusses AudioLDM2's generation-length mismatch, and identifies limitations of temporal-shift synchronization classifiers. Conditional-task integration is reframed as future work. The earlier limitations concerning training scale, metric accuracy and computational expense largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 revises stage-1 compute from 16 to 64 H100 GPU-days and adds component timing information and audio-baseline length-adaptation details. It omits v1's explicit bucketing ranges and 30% conditional-masking mixture. The abstract changes a promised resource release to claimed availability at a new project site, although Appendix A.3 still promises future release.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to UniVerse-1, Wan, SynchFormer and emotional talking-face work. It expands positioning against VGGSound and AudioSet by discussing their limitations for multi-event synchronization evaluation. The broader account of cascaded versus joint generation remains.

P1.justification: Most exposition and the main narrative remain, with local rewrites, terminology refinements and authorship/contribution metadata changes. Related work moves from main Section 6 to Appendix B; ethics and limitations are regrouped under Discussions, and the conditional extension moves from Appendix F to E.7.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column layout to a single-column ICLR format, extensively resizing and relocating displays. The benchmark comparison table is merged into Figure 4. New human-preference, prompt-distribution, attention and detailed-ablation displays are added, while the conditional-generation case figure is removed.

improvement.justification: The UniVerse-1 comparison and blind human study provide stronger evidence about the central quality/synchronization tradeoff, including weaker video quality. Duration and latency analyses improve practical assessment. These gains are limited by withdrawn conditional-task evidence and reporting inconsistencies: DeSync versus SynchFormer naming, and Table 3's consistency score of 1.201 versus 1.196 from Table A6's component scores.
